## Glossary of Key Terms

**GTV (Gross Transaction Value):** The total value of all residential real estate transactions closed by Compass agents in a given period; the primary volume metric, distinct from revenue (which reflects only the commission portion retained by Compass).

**Principal Agent:** An independent contractor affiliated with the Compass owned brokerage who generates GTV and accesses the Compass technology platform under an individual commission-split agreement.

**Adjusted EBITDA:** Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, further adjusted to exclude stock-based compensation and certain non-recurring items; Compass's primary non-GAAP profitability metric.

**FCF (Free Cash Flow):** Net cash provided by operating activities less capital expenditures; Compass first achieved positive FCF in 2024 and recorded $203.3 million in FY2025.

**Franchise Royalty:** Fees paid by independently owned franchise brokerages to Compass International Holdings in exchange for brand affiliation, marketing support, and technology access under the Anywhere brand network.

**Net Leverage Ratio:** Total net debt (long-term debt minus cash) divided by trailing adjusted EBITDA; management's stated target is 1.5x, against a post-merger starting position materially above that threshold.

**Actioned Synergies vs. Realized Synergies:** *Actioned* synergies are cost reductions that have been contractually committed or operationally implemented but may not yet appear in reported financials; *realized* synergies are those reflected in actual period results. Management had actioned $250M+ within 82 days of the Anywhere close but guided $200M in 2026 *realized* synergies.

**NAR Settlement:** The March 2024 National Association of Realtors settlement agreement, which restructured buyer-agent commission disclosure and negotiation practices across the U.S. residential market, taking effect August 2024; a material regulatory change affecting commission structures industry-wide.

**Compass One:** The proprietary all-in-one client dashboard launched February 2025, connecting agents to buyers and sellers in real time across search, touring, contract, and post-close phases; activated for approximately 330,000 client relationships year-to-date through Q3 2025.

**Make-Me-Sell:** An AI-assisted Compass platform feature enabling agents to identify homeowners who may be open to selling at the right price, expanding the addressable listing pipeline beyond traditional active-seller prospecting.

financials.key_finding:
Compass's financial narrative is one of the more dramatic arcs in post-pandemic U.S. tech-brokerage history: a venture-backed hypergrowth story that ran headlong into the most abrupt housing-market contraction in decades, survived two rounds of deep restructuring, and by 2025 had converted market-share gains into genuine free cash flow. Full-year 2025 revenue reached $6.962 billion—up 23.1% year-over-year and up from $5.629 billion in 2024—driven by organic agent growth of 19.4% (to 21,190 principal agents) and $253.1 billion in gross transaction value across 243,373 transactions. Adjusted EBITDA of $293.4 million represented a margin of approximately 4.2%, more than double the 2024 level, and free cash flow of $203.3 million marked the company's most consequential financial milestone since IPO, confirming that the brokerage model—stripped of its post-IPO cost excess—is genuinely cash-generative.

The January 2026 Anywhere Real Estate acquisition transformed the balance sheet and the income-statement profile simultaneously. On a standalone basis at December 31, 2025, Compass held $199 million in cash against $752 million in total liabilities—a modest debt load reflecting years of restructuring discipline. Post-Anywhere, the Q1 2026 balance sheet reflects $484 million in cash and $3.14 billion in long-term debt, as the all-stock transaction brought Anywhere's legacy debt obligations onto the Compass balance sheet. Management has committed to a 1.5x net leverage target, implying that at $200 million in realized 2026 synergies and continued EBITDA growth, debt service should be manageable—but refinancing risk in a prolonged rate environment is a material variable.

Q1 2026 delivered the first quarterly GAAP net income in company history at $22 million on $2.70 billion in revenue (99% reported growth; 7% on a pro-forma combined basis). Adjusted EBITDA of $61 million and 20 consecutive quarters of organic market-share outperformance—against a residential market that grew only 1.5% in brokerage GTV—confirm the operating leverage thesis. The combined 2025 pro-forma revenue base (Compass standalone $6.96B plus Anywhere standalone $5.96B) implies a full-year 2026 combined revenue run rate in excess of $12 billion at seasonal normalization, making Compass the second-largest residential real estate revenue generator in the world behind only Keller Williams Holdings.
structural_observations: Revenue base has undergone a step-change transformation: legacy Compass standalone revenue grew from $5.63B (FY2024) to $6.96B (FY2025, +23.1%), and the Anywhere acquisition adds a second major revenue layer ($5.96B Anywhere FY2025 standalone) that doubles the consolidated top line pro forma; Q1 2026 combined revenue of $2.70B is the first data point reflecting the merged entity.

Fiscal year runs calendar-year (January 1–December 31); residential real estate is highly seasonal with Q2 and Q3 generating the majority of transactions and revenue, meaning Q1 and Q4 results structurally understate full-year earnings power—the $22M GAAP net income in Q1 2026 (historically the weakest quarter) is thus a particularly meaningful profitability signal.

Margin progression has been steep but remains in early innings: adjusted EBITDA margin of ~4.2% in FY2025 is well below the 10–15% EBITDA margins achievable in a mature franchise model (RE/MAX historically runs 40%+ EBITDA margins on franchise revenue); as the Anywhere franchise revenue mix grows as a proportion of consolidated revenue, blended margins should rerate meaningfully higher.

Capital structure bifurcated by acquisition: pre-Anywhere Compass (December 31, 2025) had $199M cash, $787M stockholders' equity, and minimal legacy debt; post-Anywhere (March 31, 2026) carries $484M cash and $3.14B long-term debt—Anywhere's legacy capital structure included $4.1B in total liabilities on $5.6B in total assets—creating a net leverage position that is the dominant financial risk variable in the 2026–2028 forecast horizon.

Synergy realization pace is ahead of plan: $250M+ in cost synergies actioned within 82 days of closing (January–April 2026) against an original 2026 realized target of $100M (since raised to $200M); total long-run synergy target of $500M implies substantial multi-year EBITDA tailwind that does not yet appear in reported results.

Comparable peers for franchise segment valuation include RE/MAX Holdings (NYSE: RMAX), which generates 40%+ EBITDA margins on an asset-light royalty model, and Anywhere Real Estate pre-merger, which generated $294M in Operating EBITDA on $5.96B in FY2025 revenue; Compass's blended model warrants a sum-of-the-parts analysis separating brokerage economics (lower margin, higher growth) from franchise economics (higher margin, lower growth).

Market capitalization volatility has been extreme: COMP opened its IPO at $18/share in April 2021 and subsequently fell well below IPO price during the 2022 rate shock; the stock's recovery trajectory into 2025–2026 reflects the operational turnaround and the transformative Anywhere deal announcement, though the $3.14B debt load and integration uncertainty constrain multiple expansion.

leadership.key_finding:
Compass is a rare public company in the 2020s cohort that remains founder-led at significant scale: Robert Reffkin, who co-founded Compass with Ori Allon in 2012, serves as Founder, Chairman, and CEO and has held all three roles continuously through the April 2021 IPO, two cost-restructuring cycles, and the January 2026 Anywhere merger close. Born June 7, 1979, Reffkin holds a B.A. and M.B.A. from Columbia University and spent formative career years at McKinsey, Lazard, the White House, and Goldman Sachs (ultimately serving as Chief of Staff to the President and COO). At the IPO, Reffkin's Class C common stock and Class A holdings represented approximately 47% of outstanding voting power, a governance structure that insulates long-term strategic decisions from short-term shareholder pressure—and that has enabled the company to absorb years of losses while building the technology platform.

CFO Scott Wahlers, appointed to the CFO role effective August 22, 2025, represents a continuity appointment: he joined Compass in 2018 as Chief Accounting Officer, was integral to the IPO process, and engineered the cost discipline that produced $600 million-plus in cumulative operating expense reductions. At 53, Wahlers is a CPA with an Accounting degree from Susquehanna University and 30 years of finance and operations experience—a credentialed operator rather than a capital-markets-facing CFO.

The Anywhere merger created a notable leadership transition: Anywhere CEO Ryan Schneider and CTO Rudy Wolfs departed the company in January 2026 following close, reflecting Compass's determination to consolidate executive authority under Reffkin's vision rather than create a co-leadership structure. Timothy Gustavson, who served as Anywhere's Chief Accounting Officer since 2015 and spent 16 years at KPMG before that, was appointed Compass's Chief Accounting Officer effective March 2, 2026—bringing institutional knowledge of the Anywhere franchise infrastructure directly into the Compass finance organization.
